title: I COMMAND THIS NEW WEEK TO FAVOUR ME AND MY HOUSEHOLD BY FIRE
text: Stand to your feet wherever you are. I don't care if you are in your car, in your kitchen, on your bed, or walking into an office you've been dreading. Stand up in your spirit right now. Because we are not starting this the way we started last week, and we are not ending it the way last week ended either. Something new is being summoned. I feel it pressing against the walls of this moment, waiting for somebody to open their mouth and give it legal permission to enter. So, I'm going to open my mouth, and I need you to open yours, too. Because what we are about to walk into does not respond to silent agreement. It responds to voice. This new week must answer me by fire. >> [music] >> Say it again, louder this time, like you actually believe a week can be commanded. This new week must answer me by fire. I know how that sounds to the natural mind. A week is not a person. A week cannot hear you, cannot obey you, cannot be summoned to a witness stand and cross-examined. But I am not talking to you as a natural man this morning. I am talking to you as a spirit being who has been given dominion. And dominion means the seasons, the days, the hours themselves are not neutral, faceless containers of time. They are territories. And territories answer to whoever occupies them with authority. Last week may have gone however it went. Some of you had a week that fought you at every turn. Some of you had a week of quiet disappointment. Some of you had a week where nothing dramatic happened, but something in your spirit still feels unsettled, incomplete, unanswered. I am not here to analyze last week. I am here to make sure this week does not repeat its pattern. Let the fire fall on every territory of time before us. Kadosh esh ram, kadosh esh dolai. Let the fire of the ancient of days take possession of the seven days ahead. I want to take you to a mountain this morning. Not a mountain of struggle, a mountain of decision. 1 Kings chapter 18. Israel had been sitting in spiritual confusion for years, wobbling between two altars, unable to commit fully to the living God, unable to fully abandon him either, just existing in a lukewarm undecided middle ground that satisfied nobody, not even the people living in it. And Elijah, standing before the entire nation on Mount Carmel, said something that I believe is more relevant to your week than almost any other verse I could open with. He said, "How long halt ye between two opinions? If the Lord be God, follow him, but if Baal, then follow him." That's 1 Kings 18:21. And the people answered him not a word. I want you to sit with that silence for a moment, because I believe some of you have been living in that exact silence for longer than you'd like to admit. Not silence toward God in the sense of rebellion, but silence in the sense of indecision. Half committed to the promise, half committed to the fear, half believing the report of heaven, half agreeing with the report of your bank account or your test results or your relationship status. And that halting, that wobbling, that refusal to fully plant your feet on one side is exactly what keeps a week from ever producing a clear answer. A week cannot answer a divided heart, because a divided heart hasn't actually asked a clear question. So, Elijah did something remarkable. He didn't argue with the crowd's silence. He built an altar, he arranged the wood, he had the bullock cut in pieces and laid on the wood. And then he did something that looked, by every natural measure, like sabotage. He asked for four barrels of water to be poured on the sacrifice, not once, but three times, until the water ran round about the altar and filled the trench. He deliberately made the situation harder to explain naturally because he wanted whatever happened next to be unmistakably supernatural. And then he prayed a short prayer, not a long, elaborate, hour-long intercession, just a direct request. Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou art God in Israel, and that I am thy servant, and that I have done all these things at thy word. Hear me, oh Lord, hear me, that these people may know that thou, Lord, art God, and that thou has turned their heart back again. And then verse 38, then the fire of the Lord fell and consumed the burnt sacrifice and the wood and the stones and the dust and licked up the water that was in the trench. That is the pattern I am calling this new week into, not a wish, not a hope, a demand rooted in covenant, backed by obedience, released with confidence, expecting an answer so undeniable that everyone watching, including the parts of you that have doubted, will know without question that the Lord, he is God. Let the fire of Carmel fall on this week. Ramalesh Kadai, fire that consume wood and stone and water, consume every obstacle standing between me and my answer. I need you to notice something in that story before we move forward because it matters for how we approach the days ahead. The fire did not fall on a comfortable, easy setup. It fell on a saturated, waterlogged, seemingly impossible situation. This tells me something about your week. Maybe this week doesn't look promising on paper. Maybe there's already water in your trench, bills already due, conflict already brewing, health concerns already flagged, a deadline already looming that you don't feel ready for. I want you to understand that soaked wood has never been a problem for the God we serve. In fact, the wetter the wood, the more glory is released when the fire falls because nobody can attribute what happens next to natural explanation. This week's difficulty is not evidence that fire won't fall. It's the very set up that makes the fire undeniable when it does. Say this out loud, "My wet wood is not a disqualifier, it's a set up for undeniable glory." I feel something rising now and I want to teach a little more before we move fully into declaration and prayer because revelation must precede warfare or warfare becomes noise without direction. Jeremiah 23:29 asks a rhetorical question that carries massive weight, "Is not my word like as a fire, saith the Lord, and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?" I want you to notice the double image here, fire and hammer. Fire consumes what shouldn't remain, hammer breaks what refuses to move. This week, I am not simply asking for a gentle nudge of improvement, I am asking for the word of God to operate as both fire and hammer over every situation that has been stubborn, resistant, and immovable. There is something specific stuck in your life. Maybe it's a door that has been closed for months despite your best efforts. Maybe it's a relationship that keeps circling the same argument without resolution. Maybe it's a habit you've tried to break through sheer willpower and failed every single time. Willpower is not fire. Willpower is not a hammer. But the word of God released in faith this week carries both properties simultaneously. It will burn what needs to be consumed and it will crack open what has refused to move. Let hammer fire fall on every immovable situation. Patish esh shulam, hammer of the world, break every rock that has refused to move for months. I sense the spirit wants us to go deeper into what it actually means for a week to answer. An answer biblically is not vague activity. It's not just things happening. Things are always happening, whether they're good, bad, or neutral. An answer is a specific, relevant response to a specific, articulated request. Psalm 20:1-5 is actually a prayer the psalmist prayed over someone else, and I find it remarkable as a template. The Lord hear thee in the day of trouble. The name of the God of Jacob defend thee. Grant thee according to thine own heart, and fulfill all thy counsel. We will rejoice in thy salvation, and in the name of our God we will set up our banners. The Lord fulfill all thy petitions. This is not vague well-wishing. This is a specific covering prayed over specific petitions. This tells me that vague prayers tend to produce vague results, and specific prayers tend to produce specific results. So, before we move into the deep prayer section of this encounter, I want to challenge you. Don't let this week answer you in generalities. Get specific with heaven. Don't just say bless my week. Say what you actually need this week to produce. The job offer, the test result, the reconciliation, the breakthrough conversation, the financial provision by a certain date. Specificity is not a lack of faith. Specificity is what faith actually looks like when it's mature enough to know exactly what it's asking for. I decree over you this morning the vagueness that has kept your prayers unanswered is being replaced with precision. You will know exactly what to ask for, and heaven will answer with equal precision. Let precision fire fall on every prayer life. Daba yasha kodem, fire of precision. Sharpen every request until it pierces through vague asking into exact demand. >> [clears throat] >> Let's talk about the days themselves, because I don't believe every day of this week carries the same assignment. And I want to prophetically walk through the week ahead with you, not as superstition, but [music] as spiritual strategy, the way a wise general studies the terrain before the army moves. Whatever day is beginning this week for you, I speak fire over the opening day. Genesis 1:3 says, "And God said, let there be light, and there was light." The opening day of anything sets a tone, and I decree that the opening day of this week is flooded with light clarity, where there has been confusion, direction where there has been hesitation. Whatever you begin on this first day, I decree it begins in the light, not fumbling in the dark, trying to figure things out as you go. I speak fire over the second day of this week, the day where momentum is often tested, where the initial excitement of a fresh start begins to face its first resistance. I decree that whatever tries to discourage you on the second day, whatever email, whatever comment, whatever unexpected obstacle shows up to make you question whether this week is actually different, it will not succeed. You will push through the second day resistance with strength that surprises even you. I speak fire over the middle of this week, the day that often feels like the heaviest, the farthest from both the freshness of the start and the relief of the weekend. Isaiah 43:19 says, "Behold, I will do a new thing. Now it shall spring forth. Shall you not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert." I decree that the middle of your week, which often feels like a wilderness, becomes the very place where a new thing springs forth. Some of you are going to receive your breakthrough not at the beginning or the end of this week, but right in the exhausting middle. When you least expect a river to appear in what felt like a desert. Let mid-week fire fall now. Midbar Naharash, fire of the river in the wilderness, break open the middle of this week with unexpected breakthrough. I speak fire over the closing days of this week. The days where fatigue tends to accumulate, where patience wears thin, where the temptation to simply coast to the finish line is strongest. I decree that you finish this week stronger than you started it, not weaker. Ecclesiastes 7:8 says, "Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof." I release that reversal over your week. Whatever pattern has caused your weeks to fizzle out weekly by the end, I break that pattern now. This week will end with testimony, not just relief that is over. Let finishing fire fall now. Shalom Tovacarib, fire of the strong finish, cause this week to end greater than it began. I want to shift now into a season of pure declaration because I feel the fire building and I don't want to keep it contained behind teaching any longer. Say this with me, one at a time, and let each one land before moving to the next. This week, I decree that every closed door assigned to frustrate me is forced open by fire. This week, I decree that every voice of delay that has spoken over my file, my case, my application is silenced permanently. This week, I decree that what I have been believing God for over multiple weeks finally crosses the finish line in these 7 days. This week, I decree that no scheduled attack of the enemy will catch me unprepared because I am praying ahead of the ambush. This week, I decree that my finances will not simply survive, they will increase. This week, I decree that my health will not simply hold steady, it will improve. This week, I decree that my relationships will not simply avoid conflict, they will deepen in understanding. This week, I decree that every assignment scheduled against my peace is canceled before it can execute. [music] This week, I decree that heaven's fire falls on every altar of delay, every altar of confusion, every altar of frustration erected against my file. Let the fire of God consume every contrary decree spoken against this week. Bahimalak esh, fire of the consuming God, silence every voice that dares to speak against what has just been declared. I feel led to bring another dimension into this teaching before we move into deep prayer because I want you to understand why fire specifically and not just general blessing is the appropriate request for this week. Hebrews 12:29 says, our God is a consuming fire, not a warming fire, not a decorative fire, a consuming fire, the kind that doesn't coexist with what it touches but transforms it entirely. When you ask for a general blessing, you're asking God to add something good alongside what already exists in your life. When you ask for fire, you're asking him to consume what shouldn't exist alongside the blessing in the first place. This week doesn't just need addition. Some situations in your life need consumption. They need to be burned away entirely, not managed, not tolerated, not walked around, but eliminated. There's a difference between praying, "Help me deal with this difficult co-worker." and praying, "Let fire fall and consume whatever spiritual root is producing this conflict." There's a difference between praying, "Help my finances stretch further." and praying, "Let fire fall and consume the spirit of lack operating over my income." This week, I am inviting you to stop managing what God wants to consume. Say this with conviction, "I am done managing what God wants to consume. Fire fall now. Let consuming fire fall on every situation I've been merely managing. I challenge time it, consuming fire. Burn away what I've been tolerating instead of eliminating." Now, I want to move us into the long prayer flow because everything we have taught and declared must now be pressed into the specific territories of your life. I want you to settle into this next portion, not rushing through it, letting each line find its mark. Father, in the name that answers by fire, the name above every name, we come to you this morning not with casual requests, but with covenant confidence. Because you told us in 2 Chronicles 7:14 that if your people, called by your name, would humble themselves and pray and seek your face, you would hear from heaven, forgive our sin, and heal our land. We humble ourselves now, not in weakness, but in recognition that every answer we need this week flows from your throne, not from our striving. We pray for destiny restoration this week, Father, for everyone whose sense of purpose has felt stalled, whose calling has felt delayed by circumstances that seemed entirely outside their control. Realign every misaligned step this week. Let doors that have nothing to do with luck and everything to do with divine appointment swing open. Let this be the week where scattered pieces of vision begin gathering into a coherent picture. Let no more time be lost to confusion about direction. We pray for family deliverance this week. For homes carrying unspoken tension, for parents exhausted from carrying burdens their children don't yet understand, for siblings who have drifted into distance over unresolved offense, let this week bring a supernatural softening. Break every spirit of strife that has made simple conversations turn into arguments. Let peace be restored at dinner tables, in phone calls, in the small daily interactions that either build a family up or slowly wear it down. We pray for marriage breakthrough this week. For couples on the edge of exhaustion, remind them this week why they chose each other. Restore romance where routine has taken over. Give wisdom for the hard conversations that have been postponed too long. For couples believing for restoration after separation, let this week bring the first genuine movement toward reconciliation. For those praying for a spouse, let divine connection accelerate. Let what would have taken years happen in weeks, because this is a week that answers by fire, not by the slow drip of ordinary time. We pray for financial gates to open this week. Father, according to Deuteronomy 8:18, you give power to get wealth to establish your covenant. We ask that every financial gate that has been sealed shut by delay, by mismanagement, by the enemy's interference, or by simple lack of opportunity be forced open this week. Let overdue payments arrive. Let new income streams appear from unexpected sources. Let every seed sown in faith over the past months and years finally break through the soil and become visible harvest. Let financial fire fall now. Keseph Patah Esh, fire of open gates, force open every financial door that has resisted movement. We pray for health and healing this week. For everybody carrying an unresolved diagnosis, every mind carrying anxiety that has outlasted its original cause, every physical pain that has become a familiar but unwelcome companion, we ask for fire to fall and consume every root of sickness this week. Isaiah 53:5 tells us, "By his stripes we are healed." And we stand on that finished work asking that visible manifestation catch up to what was legally purchased 2,000 years ago. Let test results this week surprise doctors. Let pain that has lingered for months begin to lift. Let energy that has been missing for so long that you forgot what it felt like begin to return. We pray against every covenant, cause, and evil altar working against this week. Father, we renounce every generational agreement made without our consent that has granted access to delay, sickness, poverty, or premature death in our bloodlines. We command every evil altar assigned to intercept blessings meant for this week to be dismantled by fire. Let dismantling fire fall on every hidden altar right now. Misbeatch natats esh, fire of dismantling, tear down every altar working against this week's harvest. >> [music] >> We pray for angelic intervention over every day of this week. Psalm 103:20 says, "Bless the Lord, ye his angels that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening onto the voice of his word." Father, release angels with specific assignments for each day. I had angels to go before us into meetings we haven't had yet. Angels to protect us on roads we haven't traveled yet. Angels to connect us with people we haven't met yet who carry pieces of our breakthrough. Let this week be marked by so much angelic activity that we look back and recognize divine intervention in moments we almost mistook for coincidence. We pray against witchcraft assigned to this week. Every manipulation disguised as concern, every curse disguised as casual conversation, every attempt to provoke unnecessary conflict or confusion, we bind it now. In the name of Jesus. >> [music] >> We decree that every meeting convened in the spirit realm to strategize against this week's breakthrough is scattered before it can execute its plan. Let scattering fire fall on every hidden gathering against this week. Puts Russia esh dolem, fire of scattering, disperse every evil gathering assembled against this week. We pray for the restoration of time and virtue this week. For time that has been wasted in procrastination, in distraction, in fear-driven delay, Father, redeem it. Let this week produce in 7 days what would have naturally taken far longer because you are not bound by the ordinary pace of human effort. For virtue and strength drained by pouring into others without replenishment, restore it now so that we do not enter this week already running on empty. We pray for divine preservation over every hour of this week. Preserve our minds from anxiety about outcomes we cannot control. Preserve our bodies from harm on every road, every flight, every ordinary commute that carries hidden risk we never think about until something goes wrong. Preserve our hearts from offense that could derail relationships worth protecting. Preserve our faith from the erosion that comes when answers seem slow. Let preservation fire fall and seal this entire week. Shammah Chatan Esh, fire of the seal, guard every single hour of this week from the beginning until the end. I want to pause here and let you breathe because this is intense sustained warfare and I don't want you to rush past the weight of what has just been prayed. Take a moment. Notice what's happening in your spirit right now. Some of you feel lighter already. Some of you feel a fresh determination rising that wasn't there when you started reading this. That is not emotional manipulation. That is the manifestation of what has just been released. I want to bring in another layer of teaching now because I sense there is something specific I need to address about waiting for an answer. Habakkuk 2:3 says, "For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak and not lie. Though it tarry, wait for it because it will surely come. It will not tarry." I want you to notice the tension in that verse. It says the vision will tarry and in the very same breath it says it will not tarry. How can both be true? I believe this reveals something about the nature of divine timing versus human perception. From your seat, waiting for an answer, it can genuinely feel like tarrying, like delay, like the promise is taking far longer than it reasonably should. But from heaven's vantage point, watching the appointed time approach with perfect precision, there is no delay at all. Everything is arriving exactly on schedule. This week, I want you to hold both truths simultaneously. It is okay to acknowledge that the wait has felt long. That's honest, and God is not offended by your honesty. But I also want you to receive by faith that what feels like tarrying from your seat is actually precision timing from heaven's seat, and this week may very well be the appointed time you've been waiting for. Let appointed time fire fall on every delayed promise. More words man ashrai, fire of the appointed time, cause every delayed promise to arrive precisely on schedule this week. There is somebody reading this whose patience is genuinely running thin, and I don't want to dismiss that with a quick scripture and move on. I want to sit with you for a moment. You have prayed, you have believed, you have done everything you know to do, and the answer still hasn't come. And every fresh week that starts without resolution makes the waiting feel a little heavier than the last. I want to remind you that James 5:16 says, "The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much." Notice the word effectual. It doesn't say every prayer instantly produces visible results the moment is spoken. It says [clears throat] fervent sustained righteous prayer accomplishes much over time, even when the much isn't immediately visible. Your persistence has not been wasted. Every prayer you've prayed in the seasons that felt unanswered has been accumulating in the spirit realm building toward a tipping point. I decree that this week is that tipping point for somebody who has been on the edge of breakthrough for what has felt like an unbearably long time. Let tipping point fire fall now. Rof shana eish kodem, fire of accumulated breakthrough cause the tipping point to arrive this week for everyone who has waited long. I sense the spirit wants to move now into something specific about spiritual authority because I don't want anyone walking away from this encounter thinking that fire simply falls automatically without any posture required from us. Luke 12:49 records Jesus saying, "I am come to send fire on the earth and what will I if it be already kindled?" I find that phrase fascinating. If it be already kindled, it suggests that fire, once sent, requires a receiving environment, it requires kindling. Something ready to catch and sustain what has been released. This week, I want to ask you honestly, are you kindling or are you wet wood that refuses to catch no matter how much fire I send your way? Kindling looks like obedience even when you don't feel like it. Kindling looks like showing up to the opportunity even when fear says stay home. Kindling looks like forgiving even when the offense is still raw. Kindling looks like giving even when your account is tight. Fire is being sent toward you this week, but I need you to examine your own posture. Is there anything you're doing or refusing to do that would cause the fire to hit you and simply slide off without catching. I decree over every willing heart reading this you are dry kindling this week fully prepared to catch and sustain whatever fire heaven sends your way. Whatever posture of obedience is required, grace is being released for you to walk in it without hesitation. Let readiness fire fall and prepare every heart to receive. Edz Yavish esh chai, fire of readiness turn every heart into dry kindling prepared to catch what heaven sends. I want to bring in a specific word now for those in transition because I sense there's somebody whose entire week is going to be defined by a decision that has been sitting on resolved for far too long. Maybe it's a job you need to either commit to or walk away from. Maybe it's a relationship you need to either fully invest in or release. Maybe it's a location, a business idea, a ministry assignment that has been sitting in the maybe someday category when it actually needs a yes or no this week. Malachi 3:6 says, "For I am the Lord, I change not." God's unchanging nature is not just a comfort, it's also an invitation to stability in your own decision making. You cannot build anything lasting while operating from a place of constant indecision because indecision itself is a kind of instability that mirrors nothing about the character of the God you serve. I decree this week every prolonged indecision in your life comes to a clear resolution. Not necessarily the resolution you originally wanted but a clear one because clarity itself is a form of answered prayer even when the answer isn't the one you were hoping for. Let decision fire fall on every unresolved crossroads. Bakabaru esh, fire of decision bring clarity to every crossroads has remained unresolved too long. Now, I want to return to declaration because I feel the momentum building again and I don't want to lose it in extended teaching. Say this out loud one after another, letting your voice carry the authority of someone who has already seen the outcome in the spirit. I decree this week answers me with clarity, not confusion. I decree this week answers me with breakthrough, not more delay. I decree this week answers me with provision, not more lack. I decree this week answers me with healing, not more sickness. I decree this week answers me with reconciliation, not more distance. I decree this week answers me with promotion, not more overlooked effort. I decree this week answers me with peace, not more anxiety. I decree this week answers me with fire, not with silence. Let every decree be sealed by the fire of heaven. Shot Hamalach Asherai fire of the sealing angel, locking every decree spoken over this week as unbreakable covenant. I feel led to address something before we move into the closing portion of this encounter because I know that for some of you previous weeks have answered you, but not the way you wanted. And there's a quiet fear that this week might do the same. I want to be honest with you rather than simply hype you up and leave you disappointed. Not every fire that falls looks like what we expect. Sometimes fire falls as breakthrough. Sometimes fire falls as a painful but necessary ending, clearing space for something better. Sometimes fire falls as conviction, revealing something in us that needed to change before external circumstances could shift. Romans 8:28 reminds us that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to His purpose. That verse doesn't say all things are immediately pleasant. It says they work together for good, which implies a process, a weaving, sometimes involving pieces that don't feel good in isolation, but contribute to a larger good picture over time. So, this week I want you to hold an open hand toward the specific form your answer might take, while holding a closed fist of faith around the certainty that an answer is indeed coming. Trust the character of the one answering, even if the shape of the answer surprises you. Let surrender the expectation fire fall on every rigid demand. Pana, left as shalom, fire of surrender, soften every rigid expectation, while strengthening every confident faith. I want to bring us into a final wave of prophetic utterance now, because I sense the spirit has specific words for specific situations before we close this encounter. There is somebody who has an interview or a major conversation happening within the next few days. I hear the spirit saying, "You have already been chosen before you walk into that room." Walking with the confidence of someone who already knows the outcome. There is somebody who has been quietly grieving a loss that others have already moved on from. I hear the spirit saying, "I have not forgotten your grief just because time has passed for everyone else." This week brings unexpected comfort in a form you did not request, but desperately need. There is somebody whose bank account has been sending you into panic every time you check it. I hear the spirit saying, "Look again by the end of this week." What looked impossible is being rearranged even now. There is somebody who has been praying for a specific person's salvation for years, feeling like the prayers are hitting a wall. I hear the spirit saying the wall is cracking, even if you cannot see it yet. Do not stop praying now. You are closer than you think. There is somebody who made a decision recently that you've been secretly regretting, wondering if you heard God correctly. I hear the spirit saying, "Be still." The fruit of that decision has not fully ripened yet. And what looks premature now will look wise in hindsight. There is somebody whose body has felt strange, unexplained symptoms lately, that you've been afraid to get checked. I hear the spirit saying, "Go this week. Don't delay it out of fear. Whatever it is, it is being caught in time." There is somebody who has been carrying the full weight of a family's finances alone, exhausted by the responsibility. I hear the spirit saying, "Help is coming from a source you did not expect, and it is coming this week." There is somebody who has stopped believing that ministry, business, or creative dreams from years ago will ever come to pass. I hear the spirit saying, "The door you thought was permanently shut is being reopened, not through your effort this time, but through a connection you didn't orchestrate." There is somebody who woke up this morning with a strange, unexplainable sense that something is about to shift. I confirm that word right now. You are not imagining it, you are discerning it correctly. Let every word released find its assigned target this week. Rhema barak shalem, fire of confirmation. Let every prophetic word spoken settle exactly where it is needed. I I to close with a return to the mountain, because I don't want you to walk away from this encounter only remembering the fire and forgetting the posture that invited it. Elijah didn't simply demand fire out of entitlement. He built an altar. He arranged everything in order. He prayed a short, focused, faith-filled prayer rooted in God's covenant faithfulness, not in his own worthiness. And notice something remarkable. After the fire fell and consumed everything on the altar including the water in the trench, the very next thing that happened was rain. 1 Kings 18:45 tells us the heaven was black with clouds and wind and there was a great rain. The fire that answered by consuming was immediately followed by the rain that answered by refreshing. This is the pattern I want you to carry into this week. Fire first consuming, dismantling, breaking through everything that has resisted movement. And then rain refreshing, restoring, watering what the fire has cleared so that new growth can begin. Don't be surprised if this week brings both. A hard, fiery breakthrough moment followed by an unexpected season of refreshing you didn't know you needed. Let rain fire fall refreshing after breakthrough. Geshem barak tov, fire that becomes rain, refresh every place that has just been cleared by breakthrough. As we close, I want you to take one final posture with me. Not kneeling in exhaustion, but standing in expectation. The way someone stands at a door they know is about to open. This week is not neutral. It has already been marked, already been assigned, already been positioned to answer the cry that has been building in your spirit for longer than you'd like to admit. You are not walking into this next 7 days uncertain of the outcome. You are walking in with a decree already released, a fire already summoned, an altar already built and soaked and set ablaze in the spirit realm before the first hour of this week even begins in the natural. Say this one final time and let it be the last word you carry from this encounter into everything that follows. This new week must answer me by fire, not by accident, not by chance, not by the slow drip of ordinary time, by fire, undeniable, unmistakable, unstoppable fire falling exactly where I have need of it in exactly the timing heaven has appointed so that when it is all said and done, everyone watching, including the doubting parts of me, will know without question that the Lord, he is God. Let it be so. Let the fire fall. Let this week answer. It is declared. It is sealed. It is settled. Go now and watch it happen.
